hwsec/hw#HardwareEntity.rdfs:comment: Abstract superclass of every node in the decomposition tree. Do not instantiate directly; use one of the five concrete levels: System, Subsystem, Component, SubComponent, or Element.

hwsec/hw#System.rdfs:comment: The complete device or product under assessment. Root of the decomposition tree. One instance per assessment scope.

hwsec/hw#Subsystem.rdfs:comment: A functional grouping of components within a System. Subsystems correspond to major architectural partitions — typically aligned with power domains, security domains, or functional roles.

hwsec/hw#Component.rdfs:comment: A discrete physical or logical unit within a Subsystem. Typically corresponds to a single IC, SoC, module, or clearly bounded IP block.

hwsec/hw#SubComponent.rdfs:comment: A named functional block within a Component, corresponding to an IP core or well-defined internal unit. Does not necessarily have a separate die or package.

hwsec/hw#Element.rdfs:comment: Atomic unit of decomposition — no further hardware breakdown is meaningful at this level. Typically a register, bit field, fuse row, key slot, or interrupt line.

hwsec/hw#Interface.rdfs:comment: Abstract superclass for communication boundaries between HardwareEntities, or between the device and the external world. Interfaces are the primary attack surface entry points and trust boundary crossings.

hwsec/hw#PhysicalInterface.rdfs:comment: A physical connector, pin header, or test pad that provides direct hardware access. Typically requires physical proximity to exploit.

hwsec/hw#LogicalInterface.rdfs:comment: A software-visible boundary exposed by a HardwareEntity — typically a register map, shared memory region, hypervisor call gate, or bootloader command interface.

hwsec/hw#NetworkInterface.rdfs:comment: A network-facing interface that may be reachable without physical access. Includes both wired and wireless technologies.

hwsec/hw#Firmware.rdfs:comment: Software stored in and executed on a HardwareEntity. Linked to an entity via hw:hasFirmware; not a subclass of HardwareEntity. Represents a versioned software artefact for analysis purposes.

hwsec/hw#TrustBoundary.rdfs:comment: A boundary across which privilege or trust level changes. Defines the enforcement mechanism separating high-trust from low-trust execution contexts.

hwsec/sec#SecurityProperty.rdfs:comment: Abstract superclass for all security annotations. Associated with HardwareEntity instances via hw:hasSecurityProperty. Do not instantiate directly.

hwsec/sec#AttackSurface.rdfs:comment: Characterises how and from where an attacker can reach a HardwareEntity — covering access vector, authentication requirements, and remote exploitability. Individual instances link to ATT&CK techniques and CAPEC attack patterns.

hwsec/sec#DebugAccess.rdfs:comment: Describes debug and diagnostic interfaces present on a HardwareEntity that may expose privileged access beyond normal operational channels. Captures the current lock state and known bypass techniques.

hwsec/sec#SideChannel.rdfs:comment: Describes an information leakage path that arises from physical implementation properties rather than logical design flaws. Covers timing, power, electromagnetic, and acoustic channels.

hwsec/sec#FaultInjection.rdfs:comment: Describes susceptibility to externally induced faults (glitching) that alter the device's intended behaviour. Covers voltage glitching, clock glitching, laser fault injection, and electromagnetic fault injection.

hwsec/sec#Vulnerability.rdfs:comment: A specific weakness instance present in a HardwareEntity. Linkable to a CWE weakness class and one or more CVE entries. Supports CVSS v3.1 base scoring.

hwsec/sec#Countermeasure.rdfs:comment: A defensive control applied to or protecting a HardwareEntity. Instances link to D3FEND defensive technique IRIs for structured representation compatible with the MITRE ecosystem.

hwsec/sec#ThreatModel.rdfs:comment: A scoped threat model entry associated with a HardwareEntity, capturing the assumed adversary capability and the identified threat scenario.

hwsec/hw#hasSubsystem.rdfs:comment: Associates a System with one or more Subsystems.

hwsec/hw#hasComponent.rdfs:comment: Associates a Subsystem with one or more Components.

hwsec/hw#hasSubComponent.rdfs:comment: Associates a Component with one or more SubComponents.

hwsec/hw#hasElement.rdfs:comment: Associates a SubComponent with one or more Elements.

hwsec/hw#hasInterface.rdfs:comment: Associates any HardwareEntity with an Interface it exposes.

hwsec/hw#hasFirmware.rdfs:comment: Associates a HardwareEntity with Firmware that it stores or executes.

hwsec/hw#hasTrustBoundary.rdfs:comment: Associates a HardwareEntity with a TrustBoundary that it enforces or participates in.

hwsec/hw#hasSecurityProperty.rdfs:comment: Associates any HardwareEntity with a security annotation (AttackSurface, Vulnerability, Countermeasure, etc.).

hwsec/hw#crossesTrustBoundary.rdfs:comment: Indicates that an Interface crosses a named TrustBoundary.

hwsec/hw#interactsWith.rdfs:comment: Symmetric property capturing a peer communication or dependency relationship between two HardwareEntities at the same level.

hwsec/hw#physicallyContains.rdfs:comment: Transitive property asserting that one entity is physically enclosed by another. Subsumes the composition chain for physical containment queries.

hwsec/sec#mapsToATTACK.rdfs:comment: Links an AttackSurface annotation to one or more MITRE ATT&CK technique IRIs.

hwsec/sec#mapsToCAPEC.rdfs:comment: Links an AttackSurface annotation to one or more CAPEC attack-pattern IRIs.

hwsec/sec#mapsToCWE.rdfs:comment: Links a Vulnerability instance to its CWE weakness class IRI.

hwsec/sec#mapsToCVE.rdfs:comment: Links a Vulnerability instance to one or more CVE entry IRIs in the NVD.

hwsec/sec#mapsToD3FEND.rdfs:comment: Links a Countermeasure instance to a MITRE D3FEND defensive technique IRI.

hwsec/sec#mitigates.rdfs:comment: Asserts that a Countermeasure reduces the risk of a specific Vulnerability.

hwsec/sec#exploits.rdfs:comment: Asserts that a ThreatModel scenario exploits a specific Vulnerability or AttackSurface.

hwsec/hw#manufacturer.rdfs:comment: Name of the entity or company that manufactured this hardware unit.

hwsec/hw#partNumber.rdfs:comment: Manufacturer part number or component identifier.

hwsec/hw#description.rdfs:comment: Free-text description of the entity's function in the system.

hwsec/hw#trustLevel.rdfs:comment: Ordinal trust level assigned to this entity during threat modelling. 0 = fully untrusted (external world), 5 = fully trusted (isolated, verified hardware root of trust).

hwsec/hw#cpeUri.rdfs:comment: Common Platform Enumeration formatted name for this entity, enabling lookup in the NVD. Format: cpe:/h:vendor:product:version.

hwsec/hw#notes.rdfs:comment: Free-text analyst notes or observations about this entity.

hwsec/hw#firmwareVersion.rdfs:comment: Top-level firmware version string for the system (e.g. as reported by device UI or /proc/version).

hwsec/hw#certifications.rdfs:comment: Comma-separated list of applicable security certifications (e.g. FIPS 140-3, CC EAL4+, UL 2900).

hwsec/hw#function.rdfs:comment: Brief description of the primary functional role of this Subsystem.

hwsec/hw#powerDomain.rdfs:comment: Power rail or domain this Subsystem operates on (e.g. VCC_MAIN, VCC_AON, VCC_IO).

hwsec/hw#isolationBoundary.rdfs:comment: True if this Subsystem is physically or logically isolated from the rest of the system (e.g. by a firewall, separate power domain, or airgap).

hwsec/hw#architecture.rdfs:comment: Processor or hardware architecture (e.g. ARM Cortex-A53, MIPS32r2, x86_64, RISC-V RV64GC).

hwsec/hw#packageType.rdfs:comment: Physical IC package format (e.g. BGA-528, QFN-48, SOP-8, WLCSP).

hwsec/hw#processNode.rdfs:comment: Semiconductor fabrication process node (e.g. 28nm TSMC, 5nm Samsung, 40nm UMC).

hwsec/hw#endOfLife.rdfs:comment: Date on which the manufacturer ended security support for this component.

hwsec/hw#hasSecureBoot.rdfs:comment: True if this component implements a hardware-rooted secure boot chain.

hwsec/hw#hasHardwareRng.rdfs:comment: True if this component includes a hardware true random number generator.

hwsec/hw#ipBlock.rdfs:comment: Name or identifier of the silicon IP block (e.g. ARM Cortex-M33, Synopsys DWC USB3, Cadence PCIe Gen3).

hwsec/hw#clockDomain.rdfs:comment: Clock source or domain this block operates in (e.g. APLL_CLK, XTAL_32K, AXI_BUS_CLK).

hwsec/hw#privilegeLevel.rdfs:comment: Minimum privilege level required to access or control this block (e.g. EL3, EL1, Ring0, SecureWorld, UserMode).

hwsec/hw#isShared.rdfs:comment: True if this SubComponent is shared between multiple trust domains or privilege levels (e.g. shared L2 cache, shared DMA controller).

hwsec/hw#address.rdfs:comment: Base memory-mapped address of this Element expressed as a hex value.

hwsec/hw#bitWidth.rdfs:comment: Width of the register or bit field in bits.

hwsec/hw#accessRights.rdfs:comment: Permitted access modes for this Element. Allowed values: RO (read-only), RW (read-write), WO (write-only), CLEAR (write-to-clear), NONE (no-access).

hwsec/hw#resetValue.rdfs:comment: Default value of this register or bit field after hardware reset, as a hex value.

hwsec/hw#isVolatile.rdfs:comment: True if the value of this Element may change without a software write (e.g. status registers, FIFOs, hardware counters).

hwsec/hw#isLocked.rdfs:comment: True if this Element (e.g. an eFuse or configuration register) is permanently or temporarily locked against further writes.

hwsec/hw#protocol.rdfs:comment: Communication protocol used on this interface (e.g. UART, SPI, I2C, JTAG, USB 2.0, PCIe Gen3, 802.11ax).

hwsec/hw#isExternallyAccessible.rdfs:comment: True if this interface is accessible to an attacker without opening or modifying the device enclosure.

hwsec/hw#requiresAuthentication.rdfs:comment: True if access to this interface requires successful authentication before use.

hwsec/hw#voltage.rdfs:comment: Operating voltage level of this interface in volts (e.g. 3.3, 1.8, 0.9).

hwsec/hw#speed.rdfs:comment: Maximum data rate or clock speed of this interface (e.g. 115200 baud, 50 MHz, 480 Mbps).

hwsec/hw#pinout.rdfs:comment: Pin or pad assignment description for a PhysicalInterface (e.g. 'Pin 1: VCC, Pin 2: GND, Pin 3: TX, Pin 4: RX').

hwsec/hw#boardLocation.rdfs:comment: Location of this PhysicalInterface on the PCB (e.g. 'J3 header, bottom-left near SoC U1', 'TP17/TP18 adjacent to U4').

hwsec/hw#probeRequired.rdfs:comment: True if connecting to this PhysicalInterface requires a probe, clip, or soldering rather than a standard connector.

hwsec/hw#memoryBase.rdfs:comment: Base address of the memory region corresponding to this LogicalInterface.

hwsec/hw#accessControl.rdfs:comment: Access control mechanism protecting this LogicalInterface (e.g. privilege level check, MPU region, firewall rule, SMMU mapping).

hwsec/hw#sanitisesInput.rdfs:comment: True if this LogicalInterface performs validated sanitisation of all inputs before processing.

hwsec/hw#encryptionMode.rdfs:comment: Encryption protocol or cipher suite used on this NetworkInterface (e.g. WPA3-SAE, TLS 1.3, MACsec AES-256-GCM).

hwsec/hw#remotelyReachable.rdfs:comment: True if this NetworkInterface is reachable from the internet or an untrusted remote network without physical access.

hwsec/hw#wirelessRange.rdfs:comment: Approximate operational range of this wireless NetworkInterface (e.g. '10m BLE', '100m 802.11ac', '1km LoRa').

hwsec/hw#firmwareBinaryVersion.rdfs:comment: Version string of this specific firmware artefact.

hwsec/hw#hashSHA256.rdfs:comment: SHA-256 digest of the firmware binary image.

hwsec/hw#isSignatureVerified.rdfs:comment: True if the firmware image is cryptographically signed and the signature has been verified against a hardware-rooted trust anchor.

hwsec/hw#extractionMethod.rdfs:comment: Method used to obtain the firmware image (e.g. OTA download, UART bootloader, SPI clip, JTAG memory dump, filesystem archive).

hwsec/hw#binaryFormat.rdfs:comment: File or image format of the firmware binary (e.g. ELF, SquashFS, UBI, JFFS2, raw binary, SREC).

hwsec/hw#compilerFlags.rdfs:comment: Security-relevant compiler flags identified in the binary (e.g. -fstack-protector, -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2, PIE, RELRO).

hwsec/hw#boundaryMechanism.rdfs:comment: Hardware or architectural mechanism that enforces this trust boundary (e.g. ARM TrustZone SCR.NS bit, Intel VT-x EPT, SMMU/IOMMU, hardware firewall, fuse-based partition).

hwsec/hw#bypassKnown.rdfs:comment: True if a publicly known or researcher-identified bypass technique exists for this trust boundary.

hwsec/hw#boundaryBypassCveRef.rdfs:comment: URI of a CVE entry documenting a known bypass of this trust boundary.

hwsec/hw#enforcedByHardware.rdfs:comment: True if this boundary is enforced exclusively in hardware, with no software-configurable override path.

hwsec/sec#accessVector.rdfs:comment: How an attacker reaches the entity. Mirrors CVSS access vector. Allowed values: NETWORK, ADJACENT, LOCAL, PHYSICAL.

hwsec/sec#authenticated.rdfs:comment: True if exploitation requires the attacker to have valid credentials or an established session on the target.

hwsec/sec#remotelyExploitable.rdfs:comment: True if this attack surface can be exploited without physical access to the device.

hwsec/sec#complexity.rdfs:comment: Attack complexity. Mirrors CVSS attack complexity. Allowed values: LOW, HIGH.

hwsec/sec#interfaceType.rdfs:comment: Type of debug interface (e.g. JTAG, SWD, UART, I2C, vendor-specific).

hwsec/sec#debugIsLocked.rdfs:comment: True if this debug interface is locked against use without a valid credential or challenge-response.

hwsec/sec#requiresPhysicalAccess.rdfs:comment: True if exploiting this debug interface requires physical access to the device or PCB.

hwsec/sec#bypassTechnique.rdfs:comment: Free-text description of any known technique for bypassing the lock or disabling authentication on this debug interface.

hwsec/sec#channelType.rdfs:comment: Physical side-channel medium. Allowed values: TIMING, POWER, EM, ACOUSTIC, THERMAL, CACHE.

hwsec/sec#measuredLeakage.rdfs:comment: True if information leakage through this channel has been empirically confirmed (e.g. via oscilloscope trace, t-test, correlation attack).

hwsec/sec#requiredEquipment.rdfs:comment: Equipment required to exploit this side channel (e.g. oscilloscope + current shunt, near-field EM probe, software-defined radio).

hwsec/sec#faultType.rdfs:comment: Type of fault injection technique. Allowed values: VOLTAGE_GLITCH, CLOCK_GLITCH, LASER, EM_FAULT, ROWHAMMER, OPTICAL.

hwsec/sec#targetedBehaviour.rdfs:comment: The specific hardware or firmware behaviour the attacker seeks to alter (e.g. signature verification skip, AES round corruption, branch condition flip).

hwsec/sec#successRate.rdfs:comment: Empirical or estimated probability of successful fault injection (0.0–1.0).

hwsec/sec#cvssBaseScore.rdfs:comment: CVSS v3.1 base score for this vulnerability (0.0–10.0).

hwsec/sec#exploitAvailable.rdfs:comment: True if a public or private proof-of-concept exploit exists for this vulnerability.

hwsec/sec#patchAvailable.rdfs:comment: True if a vendor-issued patch or firmware update addressing this vulnerability is publicly available.

hwsec/sec#discoveryMethod.rdfs:comment: Technique used to discover this vulnerability. Allowed values: FUZZING, SIDE_CHANNEL, FAULT_INJECTION, BINARY_ANALYSIS, MANUAL_REVIEW, DIFFERENTIAL_ANALYSIS, VENDOR_DISCLOSURE.

hwsec/sec#disclosureDate.rdfs:comment: Date of public disclosure of this vulnerability.

hwsec/sec#controlType.rdfs:comment: NIST SP 800-53 / NIST CSF phase of this countermeasure. Allowed values: PREVENT, DETECT, RESPOND, RECOVER.

hwsec/sec#effectiveness.rdfs:comment: Qualitative effectiveness rating of this countermeasure. Allowed values: HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, PARTIAL.

hwsec/sec#isImplemented.rdfs:comment: True if this countermeasure is currently deployed on the target system.

hwsec/sec#implementationCost.rdfs:comment: Qualitative implementation cost. Allowed values: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH.

hwsec/sec#adversaryProfile.rdfs:comment: Description of the assumed adversary capability (e.g. 'Nation-state with physical device access', 'Remote unauthenticated user', 'Insider with production firmware signing key').

hwsec/sec#threatScenario.rdfs:comment: Free-text narrative of the threat scenario and its potential impact.

hwsec/sec#likelihood.rdfs:comment: Estimated likelihood of this threat scenario being realised. Allowed values: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH.

hwsec/sec#impact.rdfs:comment: Estimated security impact if this threat scenario is realised. Allowed values: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL.
